selected_mechanism.name: FCC cable-landing-license transfer gated by executive-branch national-security review (GCI Liberty/Quintillion)

news_trigger.quote: The remaining rules adopted in the Submarine Cable Landing License Report and Order that did not go into effect on November 26, 2025, are now effective on July 8, 2026.
news_trigger.outlet: FCC Office of International Affairs (Public Notice DA-26-684, OI Docket 24-523)

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: Before any change of ownership or control of a U.S. submarine cable landing license can be granted, the FCC must clear the application through a foreign-carrier-affiliation/security-certification rule regime (second phase effective July 8, 2026) and an executive-branch national-security review that can freeze or force mitigation on the transfer.

layers.name: Statutory delegation of licensing authority
layers.function: Vests the President's power to grant/deny submarine cable landing licenses in the FCC, making the FCC the licensing gatekeeper for every landing-station and every transfer of control.
layers.controlling_actor: FCC, acting under delegated presidential authority (Submarine Cable Landing License Act of 1921, 47 U.S.C. secs. 34-39; Executive Order No. 10530)

layers.name: FCC intake and second-phase rule regime
layers.function: Governs how transfer/modification applications are accepted and evaluated; the phase-two rules effective July 8, 2026 impose foreign-carrier-affiliation prior approval, a one-time cyber/physical security certification, and circuit-capacity reporting on the very transactions now pending.
layers.controlling_actor: FCC Office of International Affairs (OI Docket 24-523; rules 47 CFR secs. 1.70009, 1.70024, 43.82)

layers.name: Foreign-adversary substantive presumption
layers.function: Establishes a presumption that presumptively precludes grant of a landing license to any entity owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction/direction of a foreign adversary, setting the substantive standard the executive branch enforces.
layers.controlling_actor: FCC (full Commission), Report and Order FCC 25-49, released 2025-08-13

layers.name: Executive-branch national-security review (Team Telecom)
layers.function: The FCC refers cable-landing applications to the Department of State and the interagency Committee; the Committee reviews for national-security/law-enforcement risk and can lodge an objection or demand a binding mitigation agreement, which the FCC will not grant a license over. Quintillion's application (SCL-MOD-20250930-00070) was referred to State on Feb 17, 2026 and the GCI Liberty transfer-of-control applications were referred on Mar 20, 2026.
layers.controlling_actor: Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation in the U.S. Telecommunications Services Sector, chaired by the Attorney General (DOJ), with the Secretaries of Defense and Homeland Security

chokepoint.layer: Executive-branch national-security review (Team Telecom / Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation)
chokepoint.controlling_actor: Attorney General as chair of the Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation (DOJ-led, institutional role)
chokepoint.binary_decision: File an objection / recommend denial-or-mitigation on the referred cable-landing transfer vs. return no objection and let the FCC grant it
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: The FCC will not grant a submarine cable landing license transfer over an unresolved executive-branch objection. A single objection from the DOJ-chaired Committee within the referral window freezes the grant regardless of the FCC's own inclination — one named body owning a binary, not a diffuse Congress-style veto. Leverage over both the GCI Liberty transfer-of-control and the Quintillion cable-landing modification sits at this one referred node.

selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Connectivity infrastructure: GCI Liberty's pending transfer-of-control applications (referred to State Mar 20, 2026) and Quintillion's cable-landing modification (SCL-MOD-20250930-00070, referred to State Feb 17, 2026) cannot close until the DOJ-chaired Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation clears them; because Quintillion is Alaska's only U.S.-Arctic subsea fiber operator — the connectivity substrate for any North Slope or Railbelt AI data center — a Committee objection or mitigation demand in 2026-27 would delay or reprice the transaction and the Arctic backbone buildout.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Any allocator or exec underwriting an Alaska AI-data-center site tied to Arctic fiber should this week treat the executive-branch (Team Telecom) clearance of the GCI Liberty/Quintillion transfers — not the FCC's ministerial grant — as the binding closing condition, and stress-test the connectivity schedule and financing against a mitigation-agreement scenario rather than an unconditional early-2027 in-service date.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: This is a case where the visible regulator (FCC) is not the gate. The July 8 second-phase rules tighten the substantive standard, but the actual reprice/block authority is parked in a DOJ-chaired interagency committee that operates by referral and objection. For Alaska, the entire Arctic-fiber substrate that AI-data-center theses depend on runs through a single national-security veto that is invisible on the FCC docket surface — the mechanism converts a routine ownership change into a national-security clearance whose timing is not in the licensee's control.

dropped_mechanisms.name: AIDEA Mat-Su data-center land conveyance (ADL 234762)
dropped_mechanisms.reason: recent_repeat — the chokepoint is a DNR Division of Mining, Land & Water noncompetitive state-land disposal resolved by a Finding and Final Decision for a data-center use, which is structurally the same layer chain anatomized in the 07-07-02 issue (ADNR state-land disposal gate for Stak Energy). Distinct parcel, recipient (AIDEA), and vehicle (no-cost noncompetitive conveyance), but the load-bearing chain — DNR land-disposal Finding & Final Decision for a data center — is the same, so it fails the not-a-recent-repeat gate under the strict flag. (All other gates verified: news trigger real and in-window via Northern Journal 2026-07-15 and KTUU 2026-07-16, comment close Aug 19 2026.)

dropped_mechanisms.name: NSF Regional Innovation Engines — Critical Minerals Accelerator Engine in Alaska (UAF/NANA)
dropped_mechanisms.reason: diffuse_chokepoint — the sole controlling gate is the NSF TIP directorate's approximately two-year milestone review to renew toward the up-to-$160M decade path. That is a future, process-based review by a directorate, not a specific named desk/board/officer holding an imminent binary, so it fails chokepoint asymmetry. Secondary concern: the AI nexus is real (the UAF Geophysical Institute release cites 'artificial intelligence to help locate mineral deposits') but peripheral — AI is one exploration tool inside a critical-minerals funding vehicle, not the mechanism itself, raising confabulation risk for an AI-machinery column. News tie and anatomizable depth otherwise verified.
